<!--
What it does: The review's progress, step by step, as one interactive page.
  1. The 2022 World Bank NbS extraction, African studies: the scope of the
     data, how many years each paper reports an outcome for, a chosen paper's
     values over its years and seasons, and what its costs include.
  2. The practices: Pete Steward's practice vocabulary, each practice's row in
     the practice register and the changes made to follow register v0.2.
  3. The OpenAlex search.
  4. Title and abstract screening: a chart of the screening by defined practice, the
     screening for shaded perennials, and the person's QC of the model. Records
     with no abstract anywhere are left out for now.
  5. Full texts and data extraction: PDFs found, the test of the extraction
     agents against the 2022 data, the 30-paper pilot and its values, the
     extraction batches and the records left out because their practices are
     out of scope.
  6. Next steps.
Reads: data/wb_nbs_extraction_2022_cc4a.xlsx           (sheet extracted_cc4a)
       catalogues/vocab_practices.csv                   the practice vocabulary
       catalogues/crosswalk_register.csv                each practice's row in
                                                        the practice register
       outputs/03_screen/rescreen_shaded_perennials.csv records screened again
                                                        for shaded perennials
       extractions/fulltext/status.csv                  the batches, per paper
       extractions/fulltext/batch_NNN/batch_NNN.xlsx    and
                                                        batch_NNN_out_of_scope.xlsx
                                                        rows kept and moved out
       extractions/fulltext/scope_excluded.csv          records not extracted
       outputs/01_search/search_counts.csv              hits per search
       outputs/01_search/search_records_vs_wb2022.csv   DOI, open access and
                                                        the searches that found
                                                        each record
       outputs/03_screen/screen_scope.csv               decisions and QC
       outputs/03_screen/record_practices.csv           the defined practices
                                                        each record names, from
                                                        R/03_screen/tag_practices.R
       outputs/04_fulltext/fulltext_index.csv           PDFs found
       extractions/fulltext_pilot/                      the 30-paper pilot
       extractions/fulltext_v02/                        the five 2022 papers and
                                                        compare_wb2022.csv
Writes: the rendered HTML, docs/reports/progress_report.html when built with
  R/progress_report/render_progress_report.R
Flags: none. Knit in RStudio, or run R/progress_report/render_progress_report.R.
-->

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
# Money outcomes, which the outcome filter offers. Ratios and rates (benefit
# cost ratios, IRR, NPV ...) appear in the scope chart only.
COST_OUTCOMES <- c("Variable Cost", "Total Cost", "Total Cost (Unconfirmed)", "Labour Cost",
                   "Variable Cost per Asset", "Variable Cost per Unit Product",
                   "Total Cost per Asset", "Total Cost per Unit Product",
                   "Labour Cost per Asset", "Labour Cost per Unit Product",
                   "Present Value of Cost")
RETURN_OUTCOMES <- c("Gross Return", "Net Return", "Net Return (Unconfirmed)", "Gross Margin",
                     "Returns to Labour", "Return to Labour", "Present Value of Benefit")

# The outcome the page opens on.
DEFAULT_OUTCOME <- "Variable Cost"

# Cost item columns in the extraction: yes/no flags for what a cost includes.
COST_ITEMS <- c("Seeds", "Nutrient Inputs", "Labour", "Pest Control Inputs", "Land (rent)",
                "Equipment Costs", "Tax", "Transport", "Irrigation")
COST_ITEM_SHORT <- c("seed", "fertiliser", "labour", "pest control", "land",
                     "equipment", "tax", "transport", "irrigation")

PRACTICE_LABELS <- c(
  awd = "AWD (irrigated rice)", biochar = "Biochar", ca_bundle = "Reduced tillage / CA",
  dsr = "Direct-seeded rice", feed_mgmt = "Feed management",
  nutrient_mgmt_b = "Nutrient management / ISFM", rotational_grazing = "Rotational grazing",
  silvopasture = "Silvopasture", soil_cover = "Soil cover", sri = "SRI",
  trees_in_farmlands = "Trees in farmlands"
)

COL_TREATMENT <- "#1f6fb4"
COL_CONTROL <- "#7f7f7f"
HOW_COLOURS <- c("A separate value for each season" = "#08519c",
                 "A separate value for each year" = "#4292c6",
                 "One value pooled over the years" = "#fdae61",
                 "One year" = "#bdbdbd")

# The three outcome blocks of the search (docs/synthesis/key-words.xlsx).
OUTCOME_LABELS <- c(outcome1 = "Adoption", outcome2 = "Costs, returns and incentives",
                    outcome3 = "Carbon finance")

# Where each screened record ends up, in the order the counts list
# them. A record a person checked at QC follows the person's decision.
SCREEN_GROUPS <- c(
  not_africa = "Not in Africa",
  review = "Review or meta-analysis (kept for citation chasing)",
  no_practice = "No listed practice studied",
  no_outcome = "No cost, adoption or carbon income evidence",
  other_type = "Not a field, survey, evaluation or economic study",
  practice_check = "Not one of the defined practices (practice check)",
  qc_excluded = "Excluded by a person at QC",
  title_only = "Title only, no abstract yet",
  unsure = "Unsure, for a person",
  included = "Included for full text"
)
EXCLUDE_GROUPS <- names(SCREEN_GROUPS)[1:7]
# The screening rule (R/03_screen/screen_scope.R) behind each model exclusion.
EXCLUDE_RULES <- c(
  "exclude: not in Africa" = "not_africa",
  "exclude: review (keep for citation chasing)" = "review",
  "exclude: no listed practice studied" = "no_practice",
  "exclude: no cost, adoption or carbon income evidence" = "no_outcome",
  "exclude: not a field, survey, evaluation or economic study" = "other_type"
)
```

```{r data}
raw <- readxl::read_excel(FILE_WB2022_CC4A, sheet = "extracted_cc4a", col_types = "text")

#' TRUE where any country named in the cell is in Africa ("Bangladesh/India/
#' Nepal" names three). Looked up once per distinct cell.
is_africa <- function(country) {
  cells <- unique(ifelse(is.na(country), "", country))
  hit <- vapply(strsplit(cells, "[/;,]"), function(p) {
    cont <- suppressWarnings(countrycode::countrycode(trimws(p), "country.name", "continent"))
    any(cont %in% "Africa", na.rm = TRUE)
  }, TRUE)
  unname(setNames(hit, cells)[ifelse(is.na(country), "", country)])
}

#' Years a measurement covers. The column mixes formats: 2017; lists such as
#' 2017.2018; seasons such as 2018.1 or 2018.2.2019.2; ranges such as
#' 2009-2019; and Excel damage such as 2016.2017000000001 or 2009.201
#' (2009.2010 with its trailing zero dropped).
parse_years <- function(s) {
  s <- trimws(s)
  if (is.na(s) || !grepl("(19|20)[0-9]{2}", s)) return(integer())
  if (grepl("^[0-9]{4} *- *[0-9]{4}$", s)) {
    r <- as.integer(strsplit(s, " *- *")[[1]])
    return(seq(min(r), max(r)))
  }
  if (grepl("^[0-9]{4}[.][0-9]{9,}$", s)) {
    second <- round(as.numeric(paste0("0.", substring(s, 6))) * 1e4)
    return(unique(c(as.integer(substr(s, 1, 4)), as.integer(second))))
  }
  if (grepl("^[0-9]{4}[.][0-9]{3}$", s)) {
    return(unique(c(as.integer(substr(s, 1, 4)), as.integer(paste0(substring(s, 6), "0")))))
  }
  tok <- strsplit(s, "[.;,/ ]+")[[1]]
  unique(as.integer(tok[grepl("^(19|20)[0-9]{2}$", tok)]))
}

#' The season of a single-season measurement such as 2017.2, or NA.
season_of <- function(raw_year) {
  ifelse(grepl("^[0-9]{4}[.][1-3]$", trimws(raw_year)),
         as.integer(substring(trimws(raw_year), 6)), NA_integer_)
}

#' Short text saying which cost items a cost includes, for example
#' "seed, labour; not land". `d` holds the COST_ITEMS columns of one or more
#' rows; an item counts as included when any row says yes.
items_text <- function(d) {
  v <- as.matrix(d[, COST_ITEMS])
  yes <- COST_ITEMS[apply(v, 2, function(x) any(grepl("^\\(?yes", x, ignore.case = TRUE)))]
  no <- setdiff(COST_ITEMS[apply(v, 2, function(x) any(grepl("^no", x, ignore.case = TRUE)))], yes)
  short <- setNames(COST_ITEM_SHORT, COST_ITEMS)
  out <- c(if (length(yes)) paste(short[yes], collapse = ", "),
           if (length(no)) paste("not", paste(short[no], collapse = ", ")))
  if (length(out)) paste(out, collapse = "; ") else "not recorded"
}
items_by_row <- function(d) {
  vapply(seq_len(nrow(d)), function(i) items_text(d[i, , drop = FALSE]), "")
}

practice_text <- function(codes) {
  vapply(strsplit(codes, "; "), function(p) {
    l <- PRACTICE_LABELS[p]; l[is.na(l)] <- p[is.na(l)]; paste(l, collapse = "; ")
  }, "")
}

# Africa only, from the start.
af <- raw |>
  filter(is_africa(Country)) |>
  mutate(
    years = lapply(Measurement_Year, parse_years),
    n_years = lengths(years),
    year_first = vapply(years, function(y) if (length(y)) min(y) else NA_integer_, 1L),
    year_last = vapply(years, function(y) if (length(y)) max(y) else NA_integer_, 1L),
    season = ifelse(n_years == 1, season_of(Measurement_Year), NA_integer_),
    unit = trimws(Outcome_Unit),
    value_trt = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Value_Trt)),
    value_con = suppressWarnings(as.numeric(Value_Con)),
    practices = practice_text(cc4a_practices),
    paper = paste0(Country, ": ", substr(Title, 1, 75), ifelse(nchar(Title) > 75, "...", ""),
                   " [", StudyID, "]"),
    where = trimws(paste(coalesce(Site_Name, ""), coalesce(Product, ""), sep = ", "),
                   whitespace = "[ ,]")
  )

money <- af |>
  filter(Outcome %in% c(COST_OUTCOMES, RETURN_OUTCOMES)) |>
  mutate(items = items_by_row(pick(all_of(COST_ITEMS))))
```

```{r screening-data}
#' Read only the named columns of a pipeline CSV, every column as text.
read_cols <- function(path, cols) {
  readr::read_csv(path, col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character()),
                  col_select = all_of(cols), na = "", progress = FALSE,
                  show_col_types = FALSE)
}

SCOPE_LABELS <- c(in_scope = "In scope", not_taken_forward = "Not taken forward",
                  out_of_scope = "Out of scope")
vocab <- read_cols(FILE_VOCAB_PRACTICES, c("practice_code", "label", "scope", "pilot",
                                           "crosswalk", "era_codes", "system", "definition",
                                           "comparator", "notes")) |>
  filter(scope %in% names(SCOPE_LABELS))
# The defined practices in the vocabulary's order, then the records that name
# none of them.
NO_PRACTICE <- "No defined practice named"
PRACTICE_NAMES <- c(setNames(vocab$label, vocab$practice_code), none = NO_PRACTICE)
PRACTICE_SCOPE <- c(setNames(unname(SCOPE_LABELS[vocab$scope]), vocab$practice_code), none = "")

# Each record under every defined practice its title or abstract names.
tags <- read_cols(FILE_RECORD_PRACTICES, c("record_id", "practice_code"))

# Included records naming no practice were checked against the definitions by
# a GPT model (R/03_screen/classify_practices.R): the practices it found
# replace their "none" tag, and those fitting no in scope practice are
# excluded.
practice_check <- read_cols(FILE_PRACTICE_CHECK, c("record_id", "practices",
                                                   "practice_decision"))
check_tags <- practice_check |>
  tidyr::separate_rows(practices, sep = "; ") |>
  filter(practices %in% vocab$practice_code) |>
  transmute(record_id, practice_code = practices)
tags <- bind_rows(filter(tags, !(record_id %in% check_tags$record_id)), check_tags)
check_excluded <- practice_check$record_id[startsWith(practice_check$practice_decision, "exclude")]

counts <- read_cols(FILE_SEARCH_COUNTS, c("search_id", "practice_group", "outcome", "hits",
                                          "counted_on")) |>
  mutate(hits = as.integer(hits))
search_date <- format(as.Date(max(counts$counted_on)), "%d %B %Y")

records <- read_cols(FILE_SEARCH_MATCHED, c("record_id", "found_by", "doi", "is_oa",
                                             "abstract_source"))
n_search_groups <- n_distinct(counts$practice_group)

#' One row per record, defined practice it names, and outcome whose search
#' found it.
by_practice <- function(d) {
  d |>
    tidyr::separate_rows(found_by, sep = ";[[:space:]]*") |>
    mutate(outcome = sub("^.*__", "", found_by)) |>
    select(-found_by) |>
    inner_join(tags, by = "record_id", relationship = "many-to-many") |>
    rename(practice = practice_code) |>
    distinct()
}
# Abstracts found beyond OpenAlex and the 2022 refs, by R/01_search/fill_abstracts.R.
abstracts_found <- sum(!records$abstract_source %in% c("openalex", "wb2022", "none", NA))

# A person's QC decision overrides the model's. Spelling slips ("exlude")
# are read by their first letters. An exclusion the person confirmed keeps
# the model's reason; one the person made is counted as a QC exclusion.
screen <- read_cols(FILE_SCREEN, c("record_id", "qc_sample", "qc_decision", "decision",
                                   "decision_rule", "wb_positive", "wb_africa")) |>
  left_join(records, by = "record_id") |>
  mutate(
    qc = tolower(trimws(coalesce(qc_decision, ""))),
    qc = case_when(startsWith(qc, "inc") ~ "include", startsWith(qc, "ex") ~ "exclude",
                   startsWith(qc, "uns") ~ "unsure", TRUE ~ NA_character_),
    checked = !is.na(qc_sample) & !is.na(qc),
    final = ifelse(checked, qc, decision),
    group = case_when(
      checked & final == "exclude" & decision != "exclude" ~ "qc_excluded",
      final == "exclude" ~ unname(EXCLUDE_RULES[decision_rule]),
      # A person's include stands; the practice check applies to the model's.
      final == "include" & !checked & record_id %in% check_excluded ~ "practice_check",
      final == "include" ~ "included",
      decision_rule == "unsure: title only" ~ "title_only",
      TRUE ~ "unsure"
    ),
    open_access = is_oa %in% "TRUE",
    has_doi = !is.na(doi),
    wb_africa_included = wb_positive %in% "TRUE" & wb_africa %in% "TRUE"
  ) |>
  # Records with no abstract anywhere are left out of this report for now.
  filter(group != "title_only")

screen_long <- by_practice(select(screen, record_id, found_by, group, open_access, has_doi))

#' The screening counts for one defined practice and outcome ("all" for every
#' one). A record is counted once however many searches found it.
screen_counts <- function(p, o) {
  d <- screen_long
  if (p != "all") d <- filter(d, practice == p)
  if (o != "all") d <- filter(d, outcome == o)
  u <- distinct(d, record_id, .keep_all = TRUE)
  g <- as.list(table(factor(u$group, levels = names(SCREEN_GROUPS))))
  c(list(screened = nrow(u), excluded = sum(unlist(g[EXCLUDE_GROUPS])),
         included_oa = sum(u$open_access & u$group == "included"),
         included_doi = sum(u$has_doi & u$group == "included")), g)
}
overall <- c(screen_counts("all", "all"), searches = nrow(counts), hits = sum(counts$hits))

# Included records per defined practice, and those that name none.
practice_included <- screen_long |>
  filter(group == "included") |>
  distinct(practice, record_id) |>
  count(practice)
practice_included <- setNames(practice_included$n, practice_included$practice)
included_none <- coalesce(unname(practice_included["none"]), 0L)
n_checked <- nrow(practice_check)
n_check_kept <- sum(practice_check$record_id %in% screen$record_id[screen$group == "included"])
n_check_excluded <- sum(screen$group == "practice_check")
check_cost <- sum(as.numeric(read_cols(FILE_PRACTICE_CHECK, "cost_usd")$cost_usd))
n_no_practice <- n_distinct(screen_long$record_id[screen_long$practice == "none"])
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",")
```

```{r extraction-data}
# Full texts found by the fetch.
fetch <- read.csv(FILE_FETCH_INDEX, colClasses = "character")
n_pdf <- sum(fetch$status == "ok")
n_pdf_missing <- overall$included - n_pdf

#' One extraction file: the paper's decision and the cost and return rows,
#' every column as text. Pilot files (rules 0.1) and later ones share these
#' columns.
COST_SHOWN <- c("outcome", "outcome_unit", "practice", "treatment_name", "control_name",
                "value_trt", "value_con", "measurement_year", "data_type",
                "extraction_method", "page", "locator", "quote")
read_extraction <- function(f) {
  ex <- jsonlite::fromJSON(f, simplifyVector = TRUE)
  rows <- ex$cost_return
  cost <- if (is.data.frame(rows) && nrow(rows)) {
    as_tibble(lapply(setNames(COST_SHOWN, COST_SHOWN), function(k)
      if (k %in% names(rows)) as.character(rows[[k]]) else NA_character_))
  } else tibble()
  list(paper = tibble(record_id = ex$record_id, decision = ex$decision,
                      exclude_reason = if (is.null(ex$exclude_reason)) NA_character_
                                       else ex$exclude_reason,
                      cost_return = NROW(ex$cost_return), adoption = NROW(ex$adoption),
                      carbon = NROW(ex$carbon)),
       cost = mutate(cost, record_id = ex$record_id, .before = 1))
}
read_round <- function(dir) {
  x <- lapply(list.files(dir, "\\.json$", full.names = TRUE), read_extraction)
  list(papers = bind_rows(lapply(x, `[[`, "paper")), cost = bind_rows(lapply(x, `[[`, "cost")))
}

pilot_papers <- read.csv(FILE_PILOT_PAPERS, colClasses = "character")
pilot_round <- read_round(DIR_EXTRACT_PILOT)
pilot <- left_join(pilot_round$papers,
                   select(pilot_papers, record_id, outcome_folder, title), by = "record_id")

v02 <- read_round(DIR_EXTRACT_V02)
v02_cost <- v02$cost
cmp <- read.csv(FILE_COMPARE_WB2022, colClasses = c(record_id = "character"))
# The two papers where both extractions made the same comparisons.
same <- cmp[cmp$record_id %in% c("6134030", "6137948"), ]
same_matched <- sum(same$values_matched)
same_2022 <- sum(same$rows_2022)

all_cost <- bind_rows(
  mutate(pilot_round$cost, Round = "Pilot"),
  mutate(v02_cost, Round = "2022 test")
) |>
  transmute(Round, Record = record_id, Outcome = outcome, Unit = outcome_unit,
            Practice = practice, Treatment = treatment_name, Control = control_name,
            `Value (treatment)` = value_trt, `Value (control)` = value_con,
            Year = measurement_year, Data = gsub("_", " ", data_type),
            `Read from` = extraction_method, Page = page, Where = locator, Quote = quote)
```

```{r batch-data}
# The extraction batches (py/batch.py): one status row per paper. Rows naming
# only out of scope practices were moved from each batch's workbook to
# batch_NNN_out_of_scope.xlsx (py/check_extraction.py).
status <- read.csv(FILE_EXTRACT_STATUS, colClasses = "character", na.strings = "")
sheet_rows <- function(path, sheet) {
  if (!file.exists(path) || !sheet %in% readxl::excel_sheets(path)) return(0L)
  nrow(readxl::read_excel(path, sheet = sheet, col_types = "text"))
}
batch_file <- function(n, suffix = "") {
  b <- sprintf("batch_%03d", n)
  file.path(DIR_EXTRACT_BATCHES, b, paste0(b, suffix, ".xlsx"))
}
reason_text <- function(r) {
  t <- sort(table(gsub("_", " ", r[!is.na(r)])), decreasing = TRUE)
  paste0(t, " ", names(t), collapse = "; ")
}
batches <- status |>
  group_by(n = as.integer(batch)) |>
  summarise(Papers = n(), Kept = sum(decision %in% "include"),
            Excluded = sum(decision %in% "exclude"),
            `Why excluded` = reason_text(exclude_reason),
            Checked = if (all(status == "qc_done")) "By a person" else "Second reader only",
            .groups = "drop") |>
  rowwise() |>
  mutate(`Costs and returns` = sheet_rows(batch_file(n), "cost_return"),
         Adoption = sheet_rows(batch_file(n), "adoption"),
         `Carbon finance` = sheet_rows(batch_file(n), "carbon"),
         `Rows moved out of scope` = sum(vapply(c("cost_return", "adoption", "carbon"),
           function(s) sheet_rows(batch_file(n, "_out_of_scope"), s), 0L))) |>
  ungroup()
n_batch_papers <- sum(batches$Papers)

# Included records not extracted because every practice they are tagged with
# is out of scope (py/batch.py scope); in Zotero's "2. Rejected".
scope_excluded <- read.csv(FILE_SCOPE_EXCLUDED, colClasses = "character")
scope_by_practice <- scope_excluded |>
  tidyr::separate_rows(practices, sep = "; ") |>
  count(practices, sort = TRUE) |>
  mutate(label = coalesce(PRACTICE_NAMES[practices], gsub("_", " ", practices)))

# Shaded perennials came into scope on 24 Nov 2026: their own OpenAlex
# search, and the records excluded before that name them screened again.
rescreen_ids <- read.csv(FILE_RESCREEN_SHADED, colClasses = "character")$record_id
# found_by as screened: a record the shade search found but an earlier search
# had already found was screened before, and is not new.
screen_cost <- read_cols(FILE_SCREEN, c("record_id", "decision", "qc_sample", "cost_usd",
                                        "found_by"))
shade_new <- screen_cost$record_id[grepl("shaded_perennials", screen_cost$found_by) &
                                     !screen_cost$record_id %in% rescreen_ids]
shade_count <- function(ids) {
  d <- screen_cost[screen_cost$record_id %in% ids, ]
  c(n = nrow(d), include = sum(d$decision == "include"), unsure = sum(d$decision == "unsure"),
    exclude = sum(d$decision == "exclude"))
}
shade_rescreen <- shade_count(rescreen_ids)
shade_search <- shade_count(shade_new)
shade_cost <- sum(as.numeric(screen_cost$cost_usd[screen_cost$record_id %in%
                                                    c(rescreen_ids, shade_new)]), na.rm = TRUE)
shade_unsure_sent <- sum(screen_cost$record_id %in% c(rescreen_ids, shade_new) &
                           screen_cost$decision == "unsure" &
                           screen_cost$qc_sample %in% "decide unsure")
shade_searches <- sum(counts$practice_group == "shaded_perennials")
shade_hits <- sum(counts$hits[counts$practice_group == "shaded_perennials"])

register <- read_cols(FILE_CROSSWALK_REGISTER, c("practice_code", "subpractice", "register_id",
                                                 "register_status", "register_version"))
register_version <- register$register_version[1]
register_text <- register |>
  filter(!is.na(register_id)) |>
  mutate(t = paste0(register_id, ", ", register_status,
                    ifelse(is.na(subpractice), "", paste0(" (sub-practice ", subpractice, ")")))) |>
  group_by(practice_code) |>
  summarise(t = paste(unique(t), collapse = "; "), .groups = "drop")
register_text <- setNames(register_text$t, register_text$practice_code)
```

## Where the review is

```{r at-a-glance, results = "asis"}
steps <- list(
  c("1", "The 2022 World Bank data", "Done",
    paste0(n_distinct(af$StudyID), " African studies with a CC4A practice, cleaned and explored")),
  c("2", "OpenAlex search", "Done",
    paste0(overall$searches, " searches on ", search_date, ", ", fmt(nrow(records)),
           " unique records")),
  c("3", "Title and abstract screening", "Done, checked by a person",
    paste0(fmt(overall$included), " included, ", fmt(overall$excluded), " excluded, ",
           fmt(overall$unsure), " unsure, for a person")),
  c("4", "Full texts through Zotero", "In progress",
    paste0(fmt(n_pdf), " of ", fmt(overall$included), " PDFs found")),
  c("5", "Data extraction", "In progress, in batches of 30",
    paste0(nrow(batches), " batches, ", n_batch_papers, " papers, ", sum(batches$Kept),
           " kept; ", fmt(nrow(scope_excluded)),
           " records left out as their practices are out of scope"))
)
cards <- vapply(steps, function(s) sprintf(
  '<div class="step %s"><div class="step-n">%s</div><div><b>%s</b><div class="step-status">%s</div><div class="step-note">%s</div></div></div>',
  ifelse(startsWith(s[3], "Done"), "done", "todo"), s[1], s[2], s[3], s[4]), "")
cat('<div class="steps">', paste(cards, collapse = ""), '</div>')
```

## 1. The 2022 World Bank data

The 2022 World Bank NbS review extracted costs, returns and adoption from studies in low and middle income countries. Cleaned for CC4A (`data/wb_nbs_extraction_2022_cc4a.xlsx`), it is the starting point: the papers it holds need no new search, and the papers its reviewers included are used below to test the screening.

### Scope of the data

The extraction covered low and middle income countries everywhere; this page keeps the **`r n_distinct(af$StudyID)` African studies** (`r format(nrow(af), big.mark = ",")` observations) that test a CC4A practice. Values are as extracted in 2022, in each paper's own currency and prices; nothing is converted.

### How many years does each paper report an outcome for?

Choose an outcome. The chart counts the papers reporting it by the number of years their data cover, and colours them by how those years are reported: **a separate value for each season** or **for each year** (these show change over time), **one value pooled over the years** (does not), or a single year. Tick a number of years to list those papers in the table.

```{r years}
paper_outcome <- money |>
  group_by(StudyID, paper, Outcome) |>
  summarise(
    Country = first(Country),
    practices = paste(sort(unique(unlist(strsplit(practices, "; ")))), collapse = "; "),
    unit = paste(sort(unique(unit)), collapse = ", "),
    years_covered = length(unique(unlist(years))),
    separate_years = n_distinct(year_first[n_years == 1]),
    separate_points = n_distinct(Measurement_Year[n_years == 1]),
    seasonal = any(!is.na(season)),
    first_year = suppressWarnings(min(year_first, na.rm = TRUE)),
    last_year = suppressWarnings(max(year_last, na.rm = TRUE)),
    items = items_text(pick(all_of(COST_ITEMS))),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(years_covered > 0) |>
  mutate(
    how = case_when(separate_points >= 2 & seasonal ~ "A separate value for each season",
                    separate_years >= 2 ~ "A separate value for each year",
                    years_covered == 1 ~ "One year",
                    TRUE ~ "One value pooled over the years"),
    how = factor(how, levels = names(HOW_COLOURS)),
    period = ifelse(first_year == last_year, as.character(first_year),
                    paste(first_year, last_year, sep = " to ")),
    time_points = ifelse(how %in% c("A separate value for each season",
                                    "A separate value for each year"), separate_points, 1L)
  ) |>
  arrange(Outcome, desc(time_points), desc(years_covered))

sd_po <- SharedData$new(
  paper_outcome |> transmute(Outcome, years_covered, time_points, how, period, paper,

)
htmltools::tagList(
```

### Plot a paper over time

Choose an outcome and a paper (the table above lists the papers that report each outcome; if the chart is empty, the paper does not report that outcome). **Solid blue lines are treatment arms, grey dashed lines are control arms.** Seasons are separate points within their year. A value pooled over several years is a **hollow point in the middle of its period** (hover to see the years it covers); it is not joined to other points, because it is not a value for any one year. Hover for the arm, value, year or season and the cost items.

```{r plot-paper}
# Each extracted row pairs a treatment arm with a control arm. Both become
# points; an arm compared with several controls, or a control shared by
# several arms, is kept once, and an arm used in both roles in one paper is
# kept as a treatment arm.
make_points <- function(d, role, arm, value) {
  d |>
    filter(!is.na({{ value }}), !is.na(year_first)) |>
    transmute(StudyID, paper, Outcome, unit, where, items, Measurement_Year, n_years,
              year_first, year_last, season, arm = {{ arm }}, role = role, value = {{ value }})
}
trt_pts <- make_points(money, "Treatment", Treatment_Name, value_trt)
con_pts <- make_points(money, "Control", Control_Name, value_con) |>
  anti_join(distinct(trt_pts, StudyID, Outcome, arm), by = c("StudyID", "Outcome", "arm"))

pts <- bind_rows(trt_pts, con_pts) |>
  distinct(StudyID, Outcome, unit, where, Measurement_Year, arm, role, value, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  mutate(
    pooled = n_years > 1,
    # Seasons sit within their year: season 1 at the year, season 2 a third
    # of the way through, season 3 two thirds.
    x = ifelse(pooled, (year_first + year_last) / 2,
               year_first + (coalesce(season, 1L) - 1) / 3),
    when = case_when(pooled ~ paste0(year_first, " to ", year_last, " (one value for the whole period)"),
                     !is.na(season) ~ paste0(year_first, ", season ", season),
                     TRUE ~ as.character(year_first)),
    arm_where = ifelse(nzchar(where), paste0(arm, " (", where, ")"), arm),
    # A pooled value is its own trace, so it is never joined by a line.
    line = paste(role, arm_where, ifelse(pooled, paste(Measurement_Year, value), "series"), sep = " :: "),
    marker_symbol = ifelse(pooled, "Pooled over years", "Single year or season"),
    hover = paste0("<b>", arm_where, "</b> (", tolower(role), " arm)<br>",
                   Outcome, ": ", format(value, big.mark = ","), " ", unit,
                   "<br>", when, "<br>Cost items: ", items)
  ) |>
  arrange(Outcome, paper, line, x) |>
  select(arm_where, role, when, value, unit, items, everything())

# The paper picker shows how many years each paper's cost and return data
# cover, and lists the papers with the most years first.
paper_years <- money |>
  group_by(paper) |>
  summarise(years = length(unique(unlist(years))), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(paper_label = paste0("[", years, " yr] ", paper)) |>
  arrange(desc(years), paper)
pts <- pts |>
  left_join(select(paper_years, paper, paper_label), by = "paper") |>
  mutate(paper_label = factor(paper_label, levels = paper_years$paper_label))

sd_pts <- SharedData$new(pts, key = ~paste(Outcome, line, x, value), group = "points")

# Open on the default outcome and the paper with the most separate time points for it.
default_paper <- paper_outcome |>
  filter(Outcome == DEFAULT_OUTCOME) |>
  arrange(desc(time_points), desc(years_covered)) |>
  pull(paper) |>
  first()
default_paper <- paper_years$paper_label[paper_years$paper == default_paper]

htmltools::tagList(
  bscols(
    widths = c(4, 8),
    filter_select("pt_outcome", "Outcome", sd_pts, ~Outcome, multiple = FALSE),
    filter_select("pt_paper", "Paper (years of data)", sd_pts, ~paper_label, multiple = FALSE)
  ),
  plot_ly(sd_pts, x = ~x, y = ~value, split = ~line, color = ~role,
          colors = c(Treatment = COL_TREATMENT, Control = COL_CONTROL),
          linetype = ~role, linetypes = c(Treatment = "solid", Control = "dash"),
          symbol = ~marker_symbol,
          symbols = c("Single year or season" = "circle", "Pooled over years" = "circle-open"),
          type = "scatter", mode = "lines+markers", marker = list(size = 9),
          text = ~hover, hoverinfo = "text", showlegend = FALSE, height = 460) |>
    layout(xaxis = list(title = "Year (seasons as points within the year)", dtick = 1,
                        tickangle = 0),
           yaxis = list(title = "Value (paper's own currency and unit)", rangemode = "tozero"),
           margin = list(t = 20)),
  datatable(sd_pts, rownames = FALSE, class = "compact stripe hover", width = "100%",
            colnames = setNames(c("arm_where", "role", "when", "value", "unit", "items"),
                                c("Treatment / control", "Role", "Year or season", "Value", "Unit",
                                  "Cost items included")),
            options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "tip",
                           columnDefs = list(list(visible = FALSE,
                                                  targets = seq(6, ncol(pts) - 1)))))
)
```

```{r defaults, results = "asis"}
# crosstalk has no default selection and does not link one dropdown to
# another. This script (1) sets the outcome and paper filters on load, so the
# page does not open with every outcome and paper drawn at once, and (2) keeps
# the paper dropdown to the papers that report the chosen outcome, most years
# first, switching to the first of them when the current paper has none.
papers_by_outcome <- pts |>
  distinct(Outcome, paper_label) |>
  mutate(paper_label = as.character(paper_label)) |>
  arrange(Outcome, match(paper_label, paper_years$paper_label)) |>
  group_by(Outcome) |>
  summarise(papers = list(paper_label), .groups = "drop")
papers_by_outcome <- setNames(papers_by_outcome$papers, papers_by_outcome$Outcome)

cat(sprintf('<script>
window.addEventListener("load", function () {
  var papersByOutcome = %3$s;
  var tries = 0;
  (function setup() {
    var po = document.querySelector("#po_outcome select");
    var outcome = document.querySelector("#pt_outcome select");
    var paper = document.querySelector("#pt_paper select");
    if (!(po && po.selectize && outcome && outcome.selectize && paper && paper.selectize)) {
      if (tries++ < 50) setTimeout(setup, 100);
      return;
    }
    var allPapers = Object.assign({}, paper.selectize.options);
    function limitPapers(chosen) {
      var sel = paper.selectize;
      var keep = papersByOutcome[chosen] || Object.keys(allPapers);
      var current = sel.getValue();
      sel.clearOptions(true);
      keep.forEach(function (v) { if (allPapers[v]) sel.addOption(allPapers[v]); });
      sel.refreshOptions(false);
      sel.setValue(keep.indexOf(current) >= 0 ? current : keep[0]);
    }
    outcome.selectize.on("change", function (v) { limitPapers(v); });
    po.selectize.setValue(%1$s);
    outcome.selectize.setValue(%1$s);
    limitPapers(%1$s);
    paper.selectize.setValue(%2$s);
  })();
});
</script>', jsonlite::toJSON(DEFAULT_OUTCOME, auto_unbox = TRUE),
            jsonlite::toJSON(default_paper, auto_unbox = TRUE),
            jsonlite::toJSON(papers_by_outcome, auto_unbox = FALSE)))
```

### What the costs include

For each cost item, how many papers' cost figures include it, leave it out, or do not say, across all cost outcomes (variable, total, labour ...). A paper counts as including an item when any of its cost figures does. Costs that leave out labour or land are not comparable with costs that include them.

```{r cost-items}
cost_items <- money |>
  filter(Outcome %in% COST_OUTCOMES) |>
  select(StudyID, all_of(COST_ITEMS)) |>
  pivot_longer(all_of(COST_ITEMS), names_to = "item", values_to = "flag") |>
  group_by(StudyID, item) |>
  summarise(status = case_when(any(grepl("^[(]?yes", flag, ignore.case = TRUE)) ~ "Included",
                               any(grepl("^no", flag, ignore.case = TRUE)) ~ "Not included",
                               TRUE ~ "Not recorded"),
            .groups = "drop") |>
  count(item, status) |>
  mutate(item = unname(setNames(COST_ITEM_SHORT, COST_ITEMS)[item]),
         status = factor(status, levels = c("Included", "Not included", "Not recorded")))
item_order <- cost_items |>
  filter(status == "Included") |>
  arrange(n) |>
  pull(item)
item_order <- c(setdiff(unique(cost_items$item), item_order), item_order)
n_cost_papers <- n_distinct(money$StudyID[money$Outcome %in% COST_OUTCOMES])

plot_ly(cost_items, y = ~factor(item, levels = item_order), x = ~n, color = ~status,
        colors = c("Included" = "#1f6fb4", "Not included" = "#fdae61", "Not recorded" = "#d9d9d9"),
        type = "bar", orientation = "h", height = 380,
        text = ~paste0(item, ": ", n, " paper(s), ", tolower(status)),
        hoverinfo = "text", textposition = "none") |>
  layout(barmode = "stack",
         title = list(text = paste0("Cost items in the ", n_cost_papers, " papers reporting costs"), x = 0),
         xaxis = list(title = "Papers"), yaxis = list(title = ""),
         legend = list(orientation = "h", y = -0.2))
```

## 2. The practices

The review's practice vocabulary, written by Pete Steward (`catalogues/vocab_practices.csv`; the full definitions and rules are in `docs/synthesis/01-practice-definitions.md`). Each practice has a definition, the farming system it applies to, the comparator a study must use, its ERA practice codes, and what does not count as the practice. Extraction records every value against one of these codes, and sections 3 and 4 count records by them. The number on each practice is how many records the screening included that name it (section 4 explains how). Click a practice to see its definition; practices not taken forward or out of scope are listed so they can be named as reasons to exclude.

**Following the practice register `r register_version`.** The practice register (TNC and the Alliance, [CC4A-SSA/cc4adapt](https://cc4a-ssa.github.io/cc4adapt/practice_definitions/)) is the list of practices the project has agreed, with IDs such as C1.1 and G1.1. On 24 November 2026 the review was brought in line with register `r register_version` (2 November 2026; GitHub issue #23):

- **Shaded perennials in.** Shade trees in coffee, cocoa and tea (register C3.3) are now in scope, as `shaded_perennials` (they were "multistrata shade trees", out of scope). They got their own OpenAlex search, and the records excluded before were screened again (section 4).
- **Nutrient management out.** Nutrient management / ISFM (C1.3) was dropped from the register and is not taken forward. Its records are not extracted, and its rows already extracted are kept in separate workbooks (section 5).
- **Feed management narrowed.** The register's G1.1 counts feed grown on the farm, conserved feed and cut and carry. Supplementation with bought-in concentrates is now its own sub-practice, extracted but not pooled with the rest. Treating crop residues is kept in until the register decides on it.
- **Biochar feedstock recorded.** The register leaves out biochar made from forest residues; the review records each study's feedstock and flags forest residues rather than excluding them.
- **A check against drift.** Each practice code's register row is in `catalogues/crosswalk_register.csv`, shown on each practice below. `py/check_register.py` compares the two with the published register and stops a new extraction batch when they disagree.

```{r vocabulary, results = "asis"}
esc <- function(x) htmltools::htmlEscape(dplyr::coalesce(x, ""))
field <- function(name, value) {
  if (is.na(value) || !nzchar(value)) "" else
    sprintf('<div class="vfield"><span class="vname">%s</span> %s</div>', name, esc(value))
}
for (sc in names(SCOPE_LABELS)) {
  v <- vocab[vocab$scope == sc, ]
  cat(sprintf('<h4 class="vgroup">%s (%d)</h4>', SCOPE_LABELS[[sc]], nrow(v)))
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(v))) {
    r <- v[i, ]
    cat(sprintf(
      '<details class="vpractice"><summary><b>%s</b> <code>%s</code>%s%s<span class="vcount">%s included</span></summary>%s%s%s%s%s%s</details>',
      esc(r$label), esc(r$practice_code),
      if (r$pilot %in% "yes") ' <span class="vpilot">Pilot</span>' else "",
      if (!is.na(r$system)) paste0(' <span class="vsystem">', esc(r$system), "</span>") else "",
      fmt(dplyr::coalesce(unname(practice_included[r$practice_code]), 0L)),
      field(paste("Practice register", register_version),
            unname(register_text[r$practice_code])),
      field("Definition", r$definition), field("Comparator", r$comparator),
      field("ERA codes", gsub(";", "; ", r$era_codes)),
      field("Does not count, and bundles", r$notes),
      field("Crosswalk", r$crosswalk)))
  }
}
```

## 3. The OpenAlex search

The 2022 data are not enough on their own, so the literature was searched again in OpenAlex on `r search_date`: **`r overall$searches` searches**, one for each of `r n_search_groups` keyword groups and the three outcome blocks (adoption; costs, returns and incentives; carbon finance), each combined with the Africa terms and limited to papers from 1990 to 2026. The search terms are in `docs/synthesis/key-words.xlsx`. Together the searches returned `r fmt(overall$hits)` hits; many papers are found by more than one search, which leaves **`r fmt(nrow(records))` unique records**.

Section 4 follows these hits through the screening.

## 4. Title and abstract screening

Every record was screened on its title and abstract by a GPT model (gpt-4.1-mini), following the ERA screening workflow. The model answers one question per criterion: is the study in Africa, does it study one of the practices, does it report costs, adoption or carbon income, and what kind of study is it. Code then turns the answers into include, exclude or unsure, so every decision names the criterion that set it. Papers the 2022 reviewers included were shown to the model as examples. OpenAlex holds no abstract for some records; `R/01_search/fill_abstracts.R` found **`r fmt(abstracts_found)`** of them elsewhere (Europe PMC, Semantic Scholar, Crossref and the publishers' own pages), and those records were screened on their abstract.

**Practice check.** The screening model was shown the `r n_search_groups` broader search keyword groups, not the definitions in section 2, so it also kept studies of, for example, plain manure or fertiliser rates, general irrigation or intercropping, which no defined practice covers. The `r fmt(n_checked)` included records whose title and abstract named no defined practice (`R/03_screen/tag_practices.R` looks for each practice's synonyms) were checked again by the same GPT model, against each practice's definition and what does not count (`R/03_screen/classify_practices.R`, US$`r sprintf("%.2f", check_cost)`). `r fmt(n_check_kept)` fit an in scope practice and stay included; **`r fmt(n_check_excluded)` were excluded**. A person's QC decision stands over the model's throughout.

**Shaded perennials.** When shaded perennials came into scope (section 2), the `r shade_searches` new OpenAlex searches for them returned `r fmt(shade_hits)` hits and `r shade_search[["n"]]` records not found before; the model included `r shade_search[["include"]]`, was unsure of `r shade_search[["unsure"]]` and excluded `r shade_search[["exclude"]]`. The `r shade_rescreen[["n"]]` records excluded earlier that name a shade crop or multistrata system were screened again under the new scope: `r shade_rescreen[["include"]]` included, `r shade_rescreen[["unsure"]]` unsure, `r shade_rescreen[["exclude"]]` still excluded. All `r shade_unsure_sent` unsure records were sent on to the full-text screen, where the agent decides from the paper. The model cost US$`r sprintf("%.2f", shade_cost)`.

### From search to included

**`r fmt(overall$hits)` OpenAlex hits** → `r fmt(nrow(records))` unique records → `r fmt(overall$screened)` screened on title and abstract → **`r fmt(overall$included)` included** for full text, `r fmt(overall$unsure)` unsure for a person, `r fmt(overall$excluded)` excluded.

The chart splits the screened records by the defined practice they study (the practice they name, or the one the practice check found). A record studying two practices counts under both. `r fmt(n_no_practice)` screened records studied none of the defined practices and are not shown; `r if (included_none == 0) "all of them were excluded" else paste0(fmt(included_none), " of them stay included, for the full-text screen to judge")`. Choose an outcome in the menu to see the records its searches found; hover for the numbers.

```{r practice-chart, fig.height = 7}
STATUS <- c(included = "Included", unsure = "Unsure", excluded = "Excluded")
STATUS_COLOURS <- c(included = "#31a354", unsure = "#fdae6b", excluded = "#d9d9d9")
shown <- setdiff(names(PRACTICE_NAMES), "none")
axis_labels <- ifelse(PRACTICE_SCOPE[shown] == "In scope", PRACTICE_NAMES[shown],
                      paste0(PRACTICE_NAMES[shown], " (", tolower(PRACTICE_SCOPE[shown]), ")"))
bars <- bind_rows(
  mutate(screen_long, outcome = "all"),
  screen_long
) |>
  distinct(outcome, practice, record_id, .keep_all = TRUE) |>
  filter(practice %in% shown) |>
  mutate(status = case_when(group == "included" ~ "included", group == "unsure" ~ "unsure",
                            TRUE ~ "excluded")) |>
  count(outcome, practice, status) |>
  complete(outcome, practice = shown, status = names(STATUS), fill = list(n = 0L)) |>
  group_by(outcome, practice) |>
  mutate(screened = sum(n)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(label = factor(axis_labels[practice], levels = rev(axis_labels)))
outcomes <- c(all = "All outcomes", OUTCOME_LABELS)
fig <- plot_ly(height = 620)
for (o in names(outcomes)) for (st in names(STATUS)) {
  d <- filter(bars, outcome == o, status == st)
  fig <- add_bars(fig, data = d, x = ~n, y = ~label, orientation = "h", name = STATUS[[st]],
                  legendgroup = st, showlegend = o == "all", visible = o == "all",
                  marker = list(color = STATUS_COLOURS[[st]],
                                line = list(color = "#ffffff", width = 1)),
                  text = ~paste0(label, "<br>", STATUS[[st]], ": ", fmt(n), " of ",
                                 fmt(screened), " screened"),
                  hoverinfo = "text", textposition = "none")
}
n_traces <- length(STATUS)
buttons <- lapply(seq_along(outcomes), function(i) list(
  method = "restyle", label = outcomes[[i]],
  args = list("visible", as.list(rep(seq_along(outcomes) == i, each = n_traces)))))
layout(fig, barmode = "stack", bargap = 0.25,
       xaxis = list(title = "Records screened", gridcolor = "#eeeeee", zeroline = FALSE),
       yaxis = list(title = "", ticksuffix = "  "),
       legend = list(orientation = "h", x = 0, y = 1.08, traceorder = "normal"),
       updatemenus = list(list(type = "dropdown", x = 1, y = 1.12, xanchor = "right",
                               yanchor = "bottom", buttons = buttons, showactive = TRUE)),
       margin = list(l = 10, r = 10, t = 80, b = 40))
```

### Checking the model: the person's QC

A person checked three samples of the model's decisions from the title and abstract, with the model's decision in view: a random 50 of its includes, a random 100 of its excludes, and every record it was unsure about that had an abstract. Their decisions replace the model's in the chart above.

```{r qc}
qc_rows <- screen |> filter(checked)
qc_table <- qc_rows |>
  mutate(Sample = recode(qc_sample, "check include" = "Random sample of the model's includes",
                         "check exclude" = "Random sample of the model's excludes",
                         "decide unsure" = "All the model's unsure records with an abstract")) |>
  group_by(Sample) |>
  summarise(Checked = n(),
            `Person: include` = sum(qc == "include"),
            `Person: exclude` = sum(qc == "exclude"),
            `Agreed with the model` = if (all(decision == "unsure")) "n/a"
                                      else paste0(sum(qc == decision), " (", round(100 * mean(qc == decision)), "%)"),
            .groups = "drop")
knitr::kable(qc_table, align = "lrrrr")

inc <- qc_rows |> filter(qc_sample == "check include")
exc <- qc_rows |> filter(qc_sample == "check exclude")
missed <- sum(exc$qc != "exclude")
wb <- screen |> filter(wb_africa_included)
```

- **Includes.** The person kept `r sum(inc$qc == "include")` of the `r nrow(inc)` sampled includes (`r round(100 * mean(inc$qc == "include"))`%). The full-text screen will catch more of the includes that do not hold up.
- **Excludes.** The person would have kept `r missed` of the `r nrow(exc)` sampled excludes. `r if (missed == 0) paste0("With none in ", nrow(exc), ", the share of relevant papers among all ", fmt(sum(screen$decision == "exclude")), " excludes is, with 95% confidence, below about ", round(300 / nrow(exc)), "%.") else ""`
- **Unsure.** Of the `r sum(qc_rows$qc_sample == "decide unsure")` unsure records with an abstract, the person included `r sum(qc_rows$qc_sample == "decide unsure" & qc_rows$qc == "include")`.
- **Against the 2022 reviewers.** The search found `r nrow(wb)` African papers the 2022 reviewers included. The screening keeps `r sum(wb$final != "exclude")` of them (`r round(100 * mean(wb$final != "exclude"))`%) for full text or for a person to decide.

## 5. Full texts and data extraction

### Full texts

The `r fmt(overall$included)` included records went to a shared Zotero library, which fetched the PDFs it could find. **`r fmt(n_pdf)` PDFs** are in hand; the other `r fmt(n_pdf_missing)` still need a copy, through Zotero's "Find Available PDFs" or library access.

### How the data are extracted

Each paper is read in full by a Claude Code agent, which follows the written extraction rules (`docs/synthesis/fulltext_extraction_rules.md`, now version 0.3.1). The agent first decides whether the paper stays in, against the same criteria as the screening, and then extracts three kinds of data: **costs and returns** (in the 2022 World Bank template's outcomes and cost columns), **adoption** and **carbon finance**. Every value carries its page, where on the page it sits (table, row and column, or figure panel), a verbatim quote, and whether it was field-measured, reported in a survey or modelled. Values are taken as printed; the agent does not calculate. A script (`py/check_extraction.py`) then confirms that every quote is on its page and every number is in its quote, and lists the values read from figures for a person to check by eye.

### Testing against the 2022 World Bank extraction

To test the agents against people, five papers from the 2022 World Bank data were extracted again without the agents seeing the 2022 values, and the two extractions were compared value by value. Where both extractions made the same comparisons (the Uganda tillage and Ghana legume fallow papers), **`r same_matched` of `r same_2022` values from 2022 (`r round(100 * same_matched / same_2022)`%) were found in the new extraction**; the one mismatch is an error in the 2022 data. In the other three papers the two extractions compared different treatments, and in one most of the 2022 values come from a supplementary table that is not in the PDF; the table gives the reason for each paper.

```{r compare-2022}
cmp |>
  left_join(count(v02_cost, record_id, name = "rows_cc4a"), by = "record_id") |>
  transmute(Paper = paper, `Values in 2022` = rows_2022,
            `Found in the new extraction` = values_matched,
            `Values in the new extraction` = rows_cc4a,
            `Why the rest differ` = why_the_rest_differ) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrl")
```

The test also changed the rules, to version 0.2.0: practice columns carrying the vocabulary's sub-practices (section 2), every year or season as its own row, the paper's own control in factorial trials, and the 2022 definitions of gross margin and net return. Version 0.3.0 (24 November 2026) follows the practice register (section 2): a new reason to exclude a paper, *practice out of scope*, the biochar feedstock column, and the bought-in feed sub-practice. Version 0.3.1 (27 November 2026) adds Namita's answers from checking batches 1 and 2: how to code animal fattening returns, before and after changes, values not paid in cash (fertiliser replacement, willingness to pay) and discounted cash flows, and when a paper is excluded.

### The 30-paper pilot

Thirty included records, spread across the practices and the three outcome blocks, were extracted as a pilot. The agents kept **`r sum(pilot$decision == "include")`** and excluded `r sum(pilot$decision == "exclude")` on the full text (`r sum(pilot$exclude_reason == "no_outcome_data", na.rm = TRUE)` reported no cost, adoption or carbon data; `r sum(pilot$exclude_reason == "no_defined_practice", na.rm = TRUE)` did not study a defined practice), so the screening's includes still need the full-text check. From the papers kept they extracted **`r fmt(sum(pilot$cost_return))` cost and return values, `r fmt(sum(pilot$adoption))` adoption values and `r fmt(sum(pilot$carbon))` carbon finance values**. A person checked the extractions against the PDFs. Extraction took about 11 minutes of agent time per paper (9 to 15), against a median of 30 minutes per paper for the manual extraction in 2022.

```{r pilot-table}
pilot |>
  arrange(desc(decision), outcome_folder, record_id) |>
  transmute(Record = record_id, Title = title, `Searched for` = outcome_folder,
            Decision = ifelse(decision == "include", "Kept",
                              paste0("Excluded: ", gsub("_", " ", sub("^no_", "no ", exclude_reason)))),
            `Costs and returns` = cost_return, Adoption = adoption, `Carbon finance` = carbon) |>
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
                options = list(pageLength = 10, dom = "tip", autoWidth = TRUE))
```

### The extracted cost and return values

Every cost and return value from the pilot and the 2022 test, `r fmt(nrow(all_cost))` in all. Search or filter any column; the quote is the text the value was read from.

```{r cost-values}
all_cost |>
  DT::datatable(rownames = FALSE, filter = "top",
                options = list(pageLength = 10, scrollX = TRUE, dom = "tip",
                               columnDefs = list(list(width = "320px", targets = ncol(all_cost) - 1))))
```

### Extraction in batches

The included records with a PDF are now extracted 30 at a time (`py/batch.py`), the costs folder first, each batch with its own workbook for a person to check. A second Claude Code agent reads each paper again against the first agent's extraction and lists errors, queries and missed values for the person. In Zotero each extracted paper moves into its outcome folder's "1. Extracted" or "2. Rejected", tagged with its batch and, if rejected, the reason. Rows naming only practices that are out of scope (mostly nutrient management, section 2) were moved out of the batch workbooks into a separate one; a paper left with no rows is rejected as *practice out of scope*. Rows a person drops at the check (a decision against them, or their paper excluded) stay in the extraction files as a record but leave the workbook's data sheets.

```{r batches}
batches |>
  transmute(Batch = sprintf("%03d", n), Papers, Kept, Excluded, `Why excluded`,
            `Costs and returns`, Adoption, `Carbon finance`, `Rows moved out of scope`,
            Checked) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lrrrlrrrrl")
```

### Records left out because their practices are out of scope

`r fmt(nrow(scope_excluded))` included records (`r sum(scope_excluded$has_pdf == "yes")` with a PDF) are tagged only with practices that are not taken forward or out of scope, so they are not extracted. They were moved to their outcome folder's "2. Rejected" in Zotero, tagged "excluded: practice out of scope". The list is made again after any change of scope (`py/batch.py scope`), and a record that comes back into scope leaves it.

```{r scope-excluded}
scope_by_practice |>
  transmute(Practice = label, Records = n) |>
  knitr::kable(align = "lr")
```

## 6. Next steps

1. **Extraction at scale.** Batch 3 next, under rules 0.3.1, with the two shade-crop papers from batch 2 that were rejected before shaded perennials came into scope; then the remaining included records with a PDF, 30 at a time, each checked by a person.
2. **Full texts.** Find PDFs for the `r fmt(n_pdf_missing)` included records that have none yet.
3. **Practice register.** Follow the register's open questions (crop residue treatment under G1.1, the C1.1 scope, C3.3 mapping), and run `py/check_register.py` when it changes.
